The SRT-investing methodology aims to provide investors with direct access to banks' core performing assets while offering banks an efficient way to manage their regulatory capital requirements.

"The SRT market continues to present an attractive investment opportunity which we find compelling from a risk-return perspective," said Arizona State Retirement System deputy chief investment officer Al Alaimo in a statement.
Such risk transfer deals have allowed many global banks to improve their equity ratios by shifting or transferring possible losses on high-risk loans to another party.
SRT investors promise to cover a portion of the losses and in return receive a premium, which in the European market is typically between 8% and 10% in annualised terms.
